brief: brief-d052-capacity.md: one check unchanged since 30af59c (the 'not queued' half of the helper capacity check) wants a helper row queued on a lone 16-core worker holding 3.2 cores, which D-052's lone-worker rule forbids; on a trial of D-052 it fails with 0 rows, want 1; its 4-core case and its 'not claimed' sibling pass. Options: A (give the 16-core subcase a second worker running nothing of the spec and want the row there), B (keep the check, a lone worker helps itself), C (hold the fix for a measurement).
tradeoff: D-052 said every check that passed on 30af59c passes unamended; one subcase asserts exactly what D-052 gave up, so no build passes both.
serves: JS-168 criterion 6: 'with one worker nothing changes: no helper is queued or claimed, whatever cores the worker has free'. PRODUCT.md: 'A heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors rather than stalling on one machine while others sit idle.' docs/transcoding.md: 'No helper can start with one worker.'
entry: The 16-core subcase of the helper capacity check gains a second 16-core worker running nothing of the spec and wants the helper queued for it; the 4-core subcase and the 'not claimed' check are unchanged, and the amended case still fails on a build that queues nothing. It is the one exception to D-052's 'older checks stand unamended', named in JS-168 criterion 6 and cited as D-053 in Changed guarantees; any other old check that contradicts D-052 comes back as its own brief. The three JS-168 waits return to their 30af59c text (two helpers beside the main job) as a consequence of D-052, not an amendment. Rejected: B (reopens the regression D-052 closes; no rule separating a large lone worker from it is designed or measured); C (holds a merge for a measurement, rejected in D-052 and by the owner on 2026-11-21). Given up: the check's assertion that a lone worker with the cores queues a helper for itself, by operators of one large worker with transcodeHelpers on, number unknown, who were already told a lone worker gets no helper; the dogfood's 4-core case is unchanged. Unverified when decided: whether that queued row was ever claimed on a real film or sped one (the check shows a queued row only). Data that reopens it, as D-052: a measurement of a same-worker helper reaching 1.0x on idle cores; the dogfood showing a job under 1.2x on a worker with the job's cost free and no other worker to help.
